GOLD-PRP-001.primary_findings: Meta-analysis of 18 RCTs (811 patients) comparing intra-articular PRP with hyaluronic acid for knee osteoarthritis; PRP showed better clinical scores at 3, 6 and 12 months.
GOLD-PRP-001.reinforces_existing: Supports a favourable effect of PRP over HA on knee OA symptoms.
main_limitations: Heterogeneous PRP preparation and injection protocols across trials.
open_questions: Which PRP formulation (leukocyte-rich vs leukocyte-poor) is optimal?

claims.text: Intra-articular PRP improves clinical outcomes compared with HA in knee osteoarthritis.
claims.supporting_data: Pooled analysis of 18 RCTs (811 patients).

claims.text: PRP was superior to HA in WOMAC total, WOMAC physical function and VAS at 3, 6 and 12 months.
claims.supporting_data: Pooled WOMAC and VAS differences favouring PRP at all three timepoints.

claims.text: Leukocyte-rich and leukocyte-poor PRP showed no significant difference in WOMAC or VAS scores.
claims.supporting_data: Subgroup comparison LR-PRP vs LP-PRP.

claims.text: Leukocyte-poor PRP may be superior to leukocyte-rich PRP in IKDC scores.
claims.supporting_data: IKDC subgroup favoured LP-PRP.

GOLD-PRP-002.primary_findings: Meta-analysis of 10 RCTs (~1069 patients) of intra-articular PRP versus control for knee osteoarthritis, reporting improved WOMAC pain and function at 12 months.
GOLD-PRP-002.reinforces_existing: Reinforces the favourable PRP signal reported by other meta-analyses.
main_limitations: Variable control interventions (HA or saline) across included trials.

claims.text: Intra-articular PRP improves WOMAC pain scores at 12 months compared with control in knee osteoarthritis.
claims.supporting_data: Pooled WOMAC pain at 12 months across 10 RCTs.

claims.text: Intra-articular PRP improves WOMAC physical function scores at 12 months compared with control in knee osteoarthritis.
claims.supporting_data: Pooled WOMAC function at 12 months.

claims.text: PRP showed no significant difference from control in adverse event rates.
claims.supporting_data: Pooled adverse-event analysis.

GOLD-PRP-003.primary_findings: RESTORE, a placebo-controlled RCT in 288 patients, found intra-articular PRP no better than saline for knee pain or medial tibial cartilage volume at 12 months.
GOLD-PRP-003.contradicts_existing: Contradicts the favourable PRP-vs-control meta-analyses: a rigorous RCT found PRP no better than placebo.
main_limitations: Single PRP formulation; results may not generalise to all preparations.
open_questions: Do specific PRP formulations or patient subgroups still benefit?

claims.text: Intra-articular PRP was not superior to placebo saline injection for knee pain at 12 months in knee osteoarthritis.
claims.supporting_data: Mean change in pain -2.1 (PRP) vs -1.8 (placebo) on an 11-point scale; not significant.

claims.text: Intra-articular PRP did not slow the loss of medial tibial cartilage volume compared with placebo at 12 months.
claims.supporting_data: No significant between-group difference in medial tibial cartilage volume.

GOLD-PRP-004.primary_findings: Meta-analysis of randomized trials indicating intra-articular PRP reduces pain and improves function versus control in knee osteoarthritis.
GOLD-PRP-004.reinforces_existing: A third independent synthesis consistent with a favourable PRP effect.
main_limitations: Between-trial heterogeneity in PRP protocols and follow-up.
open_questions: How to reconcile positive meta-analyses with the negative RESTORE RCT?

claims.text: Intra-articular PRP reduces pain (WOMAC / VAS) compared with control in knee osteoarthritis.
claims.supporting_data: Pooled pain outcomes across included RCTs.

claims.text: Intra-articular PRP improves function compared with control in knee osteoarthritis.
claims.supporting_data: Pooled function outcomes across included RCTs.

GOLD-GUIDE-001.primary_findings: OARSI 2019 guideline for non-surgical management of knee, hip and polyarticular osteoarthritis; defines core treatments and grades pharmacological options.
main_limitations: Guideline recommendations depend on comorbidity profile; not a single-population prescription.
open_questions: How strictly are core treatments implemented in routine care?

claims.text: Core treatments for knee osteoarthritis are arthritis education and structured land-based exercise, with or without dietary weight management.
claims.supporting_data: OARSI 2019 core-treatment recommendation for all patients.

claims.text: Topical NSAIDs are strongly recommended for knee osteoarthritis.
claims.supporting_data: Strong recommendation for knee-only OA.

claims.text: Oral and transdermal opioids are strongly not recommended for knee osteoarthritis.
claims.supporting_data: Strong recommendation against opioids.

claims.text: Acetaminophen (paracetamol) is conditionally not recommended for knee osteoarthritis.
claims.supporting_data: Conditional recommendation against acetaminophen.

GOLD-EXER-001.primary_findings: Cochrane review of land-based therapeutic exercise for knee osteoarthritis: reduces pain and improves physical function, with benefit sustained for months after treatment.
GOLD-EXER-001.reinforces_existing: Level 1 support for exercise as a core treatment (aligns with OARSI 2019).
main_limitations: Heterogeneous exercise programmes; wide variation in intensity and supervision.
open_questions: Which exercise modality and dose maximise durability of benefit?

claims.text: Land-based therapeutic exercise reduces knee pain in osteoarthritis (about 12 points on a 0-100 scale immediately after treatment).
claims.supporting_data: Pooled pain reduction ~12/100 across 44 trials.

claims.text: Land-based therapeutic exercise improves physical function in knee osteoarthritis (about 10 points on a 0-100 scale immediately after treatment).
claims.supporting_data: Pooled function improvement ~10/100.

claims.text: The benefit of land-based exercise is sustained for at least 2 to 6 months after treatment ends.
claims.supporting_data: Sustained effect at 2-6 month follow-up.

GOLD-MSC-001.primary_findings: Systematic review and meta-analysis of mesenchymal stem cell therapy for knee osteoarthritis and chondral defects, reporting improvement in patient-reported pain and function.
GOLD-MSC-001.reinforces_existing: Suggests a possible benefit of MSC therapy, with important caveats.
main_limitations: Substantial heterogeneity in cell source, dose and delivery limits certainty.
open_questions: Which MSC source and dose, if any, are effective?

claims.text: Intra-articular mesenchymal stem cell therapy is associated with improvement in patient-reported pain and function in knee osteoarthritis in pooled analyses.
claims.supporting_data: Pooled patient-reported outcome improvement across RCTs.

claims.text: Evidence for MSC therapy is limited by substantial heterogeneity in cell source, dose and delivery.
claims.supporting_data: Wide variability across included studies noted by the authors.

GOLD-MSC-002.primary_findings: Systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized trials of MSC injection for chronic knee pain secondary to osteoarthritis; evidence of benefit is limited.
GOLD-MSC-002.contradicts_existing: Tempers optimistic MSC findings: some randomized comparisons show no difference from placebo.
main_limitations: Few high-quality RCTs; short follow-up in several trials.
open_questions: Are apparent MSC benefits explained by placebo/contextual effects?

claims.text: Evidence from randomized trials supporting mesenchymal stem cell injection for chronic knee pain secondary to osteoarthritis remains limited.
claims.supporting_data: Authors' conclusion on the strength of RCT evidence.

claims.text: Some analyses find intra-articular mesenchymal stem cell injection no different from placebo for knee pain.
claims.supporting_data: Null between-group differences in some included comparisons.

GOLD-CART-001.primary_findings: Meta-analysis of 12 RCTs (659 patients) comparing autologous chondrocyte implantation (ACI) with microfracture for knee cartilage lesions.
GOLD-CART-001.reinforces_existing: Supports ACI over microfracture in the medium term for focal cartilage defects.
main_limitations: Variable defect size and follow-up length across trials.
open_questions: Does ACI's advantage persist at long-term (>5 year) follow-up?

claims.text: Autologous chondrocyte implantation shows better improvement in quality of life than microfracture at 5-year follow-up for knee cartilage lesions.
claims.supporting_data: Pooled QoL favouring ACI at 5 years.

claims.text: Autologous chondrocyte implantation shows better pain relief than microfracture at 2-year follow-up.
claims.supporting_data: Pooled pain outcomes favouring ACI at 2 years.

GOLD-CART-002.primary_findings: Randomized trial (Knutsen et al.) comparing ACI with microfracture for a single femoral condyle cartilage defect, with 2-year follow-up.
GOLD-CART-002.contradicts_existing: Nuance against ACI superiority: at 2 years microfracture was not inferior and scored better on SF-36 physical component.
main_limitations: Single-defect population; 2-year horizon may miss later divergence.
open_questions: Do longer-term outcomes favour ACI as other syntheses suggest?

claims.text: In a randomized trial of a single femoral condyle cartilage defect, microfracture showed better SF-36 physical component improvement than autologous chondrocyte implantation at 2 years.
claims.supporting_data: SF-36 physical component score favoured microfracture at 2 years.

claims.text: Both autologous chondrocyte implantation and microfracture improved clinical outcomes from baseline at 2 years.
claims.supporting_data: Within-group improvement in both arms.

GOLD-MEN-001.primary_findings: Systematic review and meta-analysis of artificial meniscus scaffolds (collagen and polyurethane) for partial meniscus injury, reporting improved clinical scores from baseline.
GOLD-MEN-001.reinforces_existing: Supports symptomatic benefit of meniscal scaffolds, usually with concomitant procedures.
main_limitations: Mostly fair-to-good quality studies; frequent concomitant procedures confound attribution.
open_questions: Long-term durability and chondroprotection remain unclear.

claims.text: Meniscal scaffold implantation (collagen or polyurethane) improves VAS pain, Lysholm and Tegner scores from baseline to latest follow-up.
claims.supporting_data: Improvement in VAS, Lysholm and Tegner across 26 studies.

claims.text: Treatment failure occurred in about 9.9% of Actifit and 6.7% of collagen meniscus implant patients over roughly 3.5 years.
claims.supporting_data: Failure 9.9% (Actifit, ~40 mo) and 6.7% (CMI, ~44 mo).

GOLD-MEN-002.primary_findings: Systematic review comparing collagen and polyurethane meniscal scaffolds, finding broadly similar clinical outcomes.
GOLD-MEN-002.reinforces_existing: Consistent with GOLD-MEN-001 on comparable outcomes between scaffold types.
open_questions: Are there subgroups where one scaffold outperforms the other?

claims.text: Collagen and polyurethane meniscal scaffolds yield similar clinical outcomes.
claims.supporting_data: Comparable improvement across scaffold types in the review.

GOLD-EARLY-001.primary_findings: Luyten et al. classification criteria for early knee osteoarthritis, requiring the absence of definitive radiographic OA plus clinical and structural features.
main_limitations: Criteria are for classification, not diagnosis; require validation across cohorts.
open_questions: How well do the criteria identify patients who progress?

claims.text: Early knee osteoarthritis requires the absence of definitive radiographic OA (Kellgren-Lawrence grade 0 or 1).
claims.supporting_data: Criterion: no definitive radiographic OA (KL 0-1).

claims.text: Classification of early knee OA combines knee pain with structural or arthroscopic cartilage findings.
claims.supporting_data: Criteria combine patient-reported pain with imaging/arthroscopic structural findings.

GOLD-EARLY-002.primary_findings: Scoping review mapping how early-stage knee osteoarthritis has been defined across the literature, finding wide inconsistency.
GOLD-EARLY-002.contradicts_existing: Highlights that no single definition is agreed, complicating comparison across studies.
main_limitations: Descriptive mapping; does not itself propose a validated definition.
open_questions: Which definition should the field standardise on?

claims.text: There is no single agreed definition of early-stage knee osteoarthritis across the literature.
claims.supporting_data: Wide heterogeneity of definitions identified across included studies.
